text:
maya: Heads up — after the Karpenter migration we noticed recurring launch-queue spikes in us-west-2 when GPU workloads scale from 0 -> ~30. Pods pending for 3-4m, SIGTERM / attach errors in logs. :eyes:
jonathan: seeing same. VPC metrics show ENI attach throttling / host network capacity errors. CloudTrail shows "InvalidParameter: Insufficient host networking capacity" for a subset of instance types.
liam: do we have the subnet IPs / ENI quota numbers handy? wondering if this is just IP exhaustion per AZ.
olivia: subnet /27 in most AZs, utilization ~82% during the spike window. trunking is enabled but attach rate still high.
maya: logs: kube-scheduler pending events + karpenter-controller trace: "failed to create node: attachENI failed: rate exceeded". Happened right after a batch of small GPU jobs landed.
jonathan: hypothesis: moving to many small GPU instances increased node churn -> more ENI usage. Also Karpenter's parallel startup default is a bit aggressive.
liam: immediate mitigations: 1) request ENI quota bump from AWS, 2) increase subnet CIDR if feasible, 3) change packing policy to binpack to reduce node count.
olivia: +1 to binpack. For inference fleets we should look at consolidating multiple micro-gpu pods onto fewer larger nodes. That reduces ENI attachments.
maya: we tried turning on provisioner consolidation earlier; it moved pods but cold-start latency still spiked. Any config recs?
jonathan: try lowering maxStartupConcurrency (Karpenter config) so we don't start hundreds of nodes at once. Also set ttlSecondsAfterEmpty shorter to evict idle nodes faster but not during scale bursts.
liam: sketch of a conservative provisioner policy to prototype binpacking and limit parallelism:
```yaml
apiVersion: karpenter.sh/v1alpha5
kind: Provisioner
metadata:
  name: gpu-binpack-provisioner
spec:
  requirements:
  - key: karpenter.k8s.aws/instance-category
    operator: In
    values: [gpu]
  consolidation: true
  ttlSecondsAfterEmpty: 300
  provider:
    maxStartupConcurrency: 8
    instanceProfile: infra-gpu
    subnetSelector:
      kubernetes.io/cluster/my-cluster: "owned"
```
jonathan: also consider preferring fewer larger instances (eg 1x A100 or 1x p4d) rather than many small ones — fewer ENIs overall. cost tradeoffs depend on utilization and packing efficiency.
olivia: small test note: switching a single job to a larger instance dropped ENI attaches by ~60% in our smoke run, but CPU/GPU time underutilized for some workloads. Need cost sim.
maya: could we run a short simulation: 1) current small-GPU mix, 2) fewer larger GPUs, 3) warmpool with reserved placeholder pods to hold IPs. Compare cost + median startup latency.
liam: running a back-of-envelope now. Quick thought: warmpool placeholder pods are hacky — kubelet evictions and taints complicate that approach. AWS now has ENI warmup features we could lean on.
jonathan: also check CNI config: aws-vpc-cni has warm IP target config and prefix-mode settings that dramatically change attach behavior. If we're using single IP per pod mode we should try prefix mode + warm targets.
maya: we got an incident alert during the spike: sre-bot posted the detection.
sre-bot: Incident alert: GPU-provisioner-queue spike detected for prod-us-west-2 at 2026-03-18T10:03:21Z. EventID=evt-1968456789. Impact: scheduling latency >180s for 28 pods.
olivia: next steps agreed: liam will run cost + IP usage sim and open an AWS quota request; jonathan will prototype the provisioner with maxStartupConcurrency=8 and binpack preference; maya will monitor cluster scheduling metrics and collect sample pod trace logs; i'll test CNI prefix-mode + warm targets in staging.
maya: post any outputs here and we can pick a remediation path. :thumbsup:
